refs.what: The bedroom carpet developed a large dark stain in front of the wardrobes during the two-year tenancy that was not present at move-in.
The bedroom wall shows new scuffed and peeling paint patches to the right of the radiator at move-out that were not visible at move-in.
A large dark brown stain is present in the middle of the living-room carpet at move-out that was clean and uniform at move-in.
After image shows dark circular burn marks on the wooden worktop beside the hob that were not present before.
The oven front was clean at move-in but is covered in grease splatters and food marks at move-out that cleaning would remove.
The bath is intact but the white sealant has developed heavy black mould along the edges that was clean before.
The living-room wall shows a few extra small nail-hole marks and light scuffs after two years consistent with normal use.

text:
Dear Landlord,

Re: Demo flat (simulated) – deposit deductions after 2-year tenancy

Thank you for your deduction list. I reply below to each item as claimed, referring to the photo evidence pack.

E1 – bedroom carpet stain in front of wardrobes: Part-accept. This is damage beyond fair wear and tear. To avoid betterment, cost must be apportioned by useful life. I accept 71%, based on 2 years' use of a 7-year life.

E2 – bedroom wall scuffed/peeling paint right of radiator: Part-accept. This is damage, not fair wear and tear. I accept 50%, based on 2 years' use of a 4-year life.

E3 – living-room carpet large brown stain: Part-accept. This is damage. To avoid betterment, I accept 71%, based on 2 years' use of a 7-year life.

E4 – kitchen worktop burn marks by hob: Part-accept. This is damage. To avoid betterment, I accept 87%, based on 2 years' use of a 15-year life.

E5 – kitchen oven grease and food marks: Accept. This is cleaning, not fair wear and tear. I accept 100% of the reasonable cleaning cost.

E6 – bathroom bath sealant black mould: Accept. This is cleaning. I accept 100% of the reasonable cleaning cost.

E7 – living-room wall nail holes and light scuffs: Dispute. After two years this is fair wear and tear from normal use. I accept 0%.

Please send invoices for the cleaning and like-for-like replacement claimed, with the above apportionment applied. If we cannot agree, I may use the scheme's free dispute resolution.

Kind regards,
Tenant
